name: Persepolis (Takht-e Jamshid)
builtBy: Darius I the Great and Xerxes I
description: Colossal terrace ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire, ancient Wonder of the Near East.
history: Founded by Darius the Great in 518 BCE as the grand ceremonial capital where tributary nations from Egypt to India brought offerings during Nowruz (Persian New Year). Burned by Alexander the Great in 330 BCE.
construction: Built upon a massive 125,000 square meter stone terrace cut into Mount Rahmat, using precision iron-clamped limestone masonry without mortar.
architecture: Showcases the Gate of All Nations with colossal winged bull lamassu, the 72-column Apadana audience hall, and the Hall of a Hundred Columns.
significance: The crowning architectural achievement of the Achaemenid Empire; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
currentStatus: Preserved ruins and bas-reliefs near Shiraz, Iran.
wonderCategory: Ancient Wonder of Architecture (UNESCO World Heritage)
wonderHistoricalContext: Revered throughout the ancient world as the jewel of Persia. Its bas-reliefs depict peaceful processions of 23 subject nations, standing as the supreme wonder of Persian imperial architecture.
